comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows Language and Cognition in the Dutch-language track. The 120 EC major includes a capstone and thesis. The remaining 60 EC include a coherent elective package and other electives.
components: Introduces scientific approaches to studying human language.
Studies how people acquire and process language.
Compares word formation and sentence structure across languages.
Studies language in its social contexts.
Uses digital tools to investigate language.
Studies the production and perception of speech sounds.
Develops research methods and statistical analysis for linguistics.
Examines sound systems and how to study them through fieldwork.
Uses experiments to investigate language processing.
Examines the internal structure of words.
Studies literal meaning and how context affects interpretation.
Examines language acquisition in relation to language structure.
Capstone Course Linguistics: Research, Writing and Reflection
Develops a research proposal and prepares students to write the thesis.
Students investigate a linguistic question and report their findings.
Choose a minor, a second specialization or approved study abroad.
Choose additional courses under Utrecht’s degree rules.

core: Linguistic structure, comparison and the scientific study of human language
Language acquisition, cognition, speech processing and human behaviour
Empirical, experimental, quantitative and digital methods for language research
Meaning, communication and language in social context
adjacent: Language, society, multilingualism, identity and mediated communication
Computational linguistics, formal language, artificial intelligence and language models
questions: How do people acquire, process and understand language?
How do language, identity and multilingual communities shape one another?
How can computation and AI model human language?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Language, cognition and communication
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the plan’s main subjects and methods.
alternatives.concept: Study how people understand and produce language. Connect psycholinguistics, brain science and philosophy of mind with the analysis of meaning, and use research methods to examine evidence about language and cognition.
progression: Brain and behavior precedes psycholinguistics. Introductory cognition and perception lead to advanced cognition, experimental statistics and evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Language, identity and public communication
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the plan’s main subjects and methods.
alternatives.concept: Study how people use language to express identity, persuade others and participate in public life. Explore bilingualism and language processing, analyze rhetoric and narrative, and use qualitative research to examine communication in social settings.
progression: Rhetoric, sociology and brain science lead into stylistics, psycholinguistics, community speaking and advanced analysis of identity, discourse and media.
alternatives.distinctness: 11 courses and 82.5 EC differ each way from option 1. Social theory, public rhetoric, narrative and representation distinguish this plan.

alternatives.label: Language data, computation and AI
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the plan’s main subjects and methods.
alternatives.concept: Study how computing can help model language. Use Python, logic, statistics and machine learning to work with text data, and connect language models with the human processes studied in psycholinguistics.
progression: Programming and data science precede machine learning, logic and advanced AI. Brain and behavior precedes psycholinguistics, and quantitative foundations lead into deep learning and text analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: 10 courses and 75 EC differ each way from option 1. 17 courses and 127.5 EC differ each way from option 2. Python, logic, mathematics, machine learning and neural language models distinguish this plan.

blocks: Both study how linguistic choices shape meaning. UCR approaches this through stylistics, dialogue and discourse.
Both examine human language processing. UCR covers experimental approaches alongside neuroscience, bilingualism and language disorders.
Utrecht introduces linguistics as a field of study.
Utrecht has a dedicated introduction to language psychology. UCR studies related processes in psycholinguistics and other cognition courses.
Utrecht compares how languages build words and sentences. UCR touches on these features in stylistics.
Utrecht studies how language develops. UCR offers broader developmental psychology and psycholinguistics.
Utrecht has a dedicated course on speech sounds and their production and perception.
Utrecht studies word structure in depth.
Utrecht has a dedicated course on semantics and pragmatics. UCR examines dialogue and language in context through stylistics.
Utrecht connects theories of language acquisition and grammatical structure.
Utrecht studies language variation in social settings. UCR approaches related questions through sociology and communication.
Both use digital methods to work with data. UCR covers general data analysis, including text data.
Both develop empirical research and statistical analysis. UCR uses examples from psychology.
Utrecht studies sound systems through linguistic fieldwork. UCR offers broader qualitative research methods.
Utrecht’s capstone develops a proposal for the required thesis.
Utrecht requires a thesis. UCR’s optional research element sits outside the scheduled degree.
This is a coherent elective package, such as a minor or a second specialization.
Students choose these electives under Utrecht’s degree rules.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Linguistics target is registered as Dutch. The Language and Cognition specialization is used because it develops the degree’s central questions about language structure, acquisition and processing. The other two specializations remain separate official directions.

selection.assessment: The three plans address distinct interests in language processing, language use in society, and computational approaches to language. All meet feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Each has a different balance of specialist language content and complementary disciplines.

notes.text: Utrecht’s degree includes a 120 EC major and 60 EC of electives. Half of the elective credits form a coherent package. Utrecht also requires a basic grammar test.
The UCR options share topics and methods with Utrecht. Utrecht has dedicated courses in phonetics, phonology, grammar and linguistic fieldwork, along with a required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how language works, how people acquire and understand it, and how it varies across communities. Utrecht offers Dutch- and English-language tracks. This example follows the Dutch track.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example focuses on language and cognition. The UCR options emphasize cognition and communication, language and identity, or language data and AI.
